The *Kalahavivādasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 11) is an exegetical text located in the *Mahāniddesa* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It serves as an extensive canonical commentary and exposition on the *Kalahavivāda Sutta* (*Sutta Nipāta* 4.11) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records two translations in two languages for this text, and notes relationships or cross-mentions with numerous canonical and post-canonical works, including the root discourse (Snp 4.11), the *Chachakka Sutta* (MN 148), the *Dīghanakha Sutta* (MN 74), the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 6.7, Kv 18.2), discourses of the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 22.25, SN 23.9, SN 35.60) and *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3.125), the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.2.1), parallel Āgama texts such as SĀ 77 and SĀ 304, Sanskrit fragments (SHT Sutta 71), and the *Abhidharmakośopāyikā* (Up 3.059) [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus documents extensive internal reuse within the Pali tradition, identifying 5,648 matching passages shared with 223 texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest reuse partners are other chapters of the *Mahāniddesa*—most prominently the *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 10), *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), and *Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 15)—as well as the *Cūḷaniddesa* (e.g., Cnd 5, Cnd 8, Cnd 23), the root *Kalahavivāda Sutta* (Snp 4.11), the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1) [DharmaNexus].
